questions.question: A is twice as good a workman as B, and together they finish a work in 10 days. In how many days will A finish the work alone?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A is twice as good a workman as B, and together they finish a work in 10 days.

**Formula used:**

If A is twice as good as B, then A's work rate is 2B's work rate.

Let B's work rate be x work/day. Then, A's work rate is 2x work/day.

Combined work rate of A and B = (2x + x) work/day = 3x work/day.

They finish the work together in 10 days, so:

Work completed in 10 days = 3x × 10 = 30x.

Work completed by A alone in 1 day = 2x work/day.

**Calculation:**

3x × 10 = 1 work (total work)

⇒ 30x = 1

⇒ x = 1/30

A's work rate = 2x = 2 × (1/30) = 1/15 work/day.

Time taken by A alone to finish the work:

⇒ 1 work / (1/15) work/day

⇒ 15 days

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: A shopkeeper has 25 litres of oil in one can and 45 litres in another can. The maximum capacity (in litres) of a container that can measure the oil of either container an exact number of times is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Quantity of oil in the first can = 25 litres

Quantity of oil in the second can = 45 litres

**Formula used:**

To find the maximum capacity of a container that can measure the oil exactly in both cans, we need to find the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of 25 and 45.

**Calculation:**

Find the factors of 25 and 45:

Factors of 25 = 1, 5, 25

Factors of 45 = 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 45

The common factor is 5, and it is the highest.

⇒ HCF of 25 and 45 = 5

**∴ The maximum capacity of the container is 5 litres.**

questions.question: The Braille System is based on:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**dots**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Braille system is a tactile writing system used by people who are visually impaired.
 
• It is traditionally written with embossed paper and consists of raised dots.
 
• Each Braille character or cell is made up of six dots arranged in a rectangle containing two columns of three dots each.
 
• The arrangement of these dots represents different letters and symbols used in written language.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Braille System:**

 
 
• Named after its creator, Louis Braille, who developed the system in 1824.
 
• Braille is used worldwide and has been adapted to different languages.
 
• It includes not just letters and punctuation, but also numeric symbols, musical notation, and computer notation.
 
• Learning Braille allows visually impaired individuals to read and write independently, providing access to education, employment, and information.
 
 
 
• **Louis Braille:**
 
 
• Born in 1809 in France, Louis Braille lost his sight at a young age due to an accident.
 
• He was a student at the Royal Institute for Blind Youth in Paris where he developed the Braille system.
 
• The system was based on a tactile military code called "night writing" developed by Charles Barbier.
 
• Louis Braille's system was officially adopted by the Institute in 1854, two years after his death.
 
 
 
• **Usage of Braille:**
 
 
• Braille is used in many areas including education, literature, and public spaces.
 
• Books, menus, signs, and even currency in some countries have Braille for accessibility.
 
• Technology advancements have led to Braille displays and printers, which allow visually impaired individuals to interact with digital information.
 
• Braille literacy is crucial for the independence and empowerment of individuals with visual impairments.
 
 
 
• **Modern Adaptations:**
 
 
• Electronic Braille devices like Braille e-books, Braille watches, and Braille note-takers are becoming more common.
 
• These devices help in accessing digital content and communication for visually impaired individuals.
 
• Braille transcription services convert printed text into Braille for educational and informational purposes.
 
• Efforts continue globally to promote Braille literacy and ensure accessibility in public and private sectors.

questions.question: For how many years are the judges of the International Court of Justice elected?

__
 
• The judges of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) are elected for a term of **9 years**.
 
• They can be re-elected if they continue to meet the qualifications required.

• The judges are elected by the United Nations General Assembly and the Security Council.

• It was established in June 1945 by the Charter of the United Nations and began work in April 1946.
 
• The court's role is to settle legal disputes submitted to it by states and to give advisory opinions on legal questions referred to it by authorized UN organs and specialized agencies.
 
• The ICJ is located in The Hague, Netherlands.
 
 
 
• **Election Process**
 
 
• Judges are elected by the United Nations General Assembly and Security Council, where candidates must receive an absolute majority in both bodies.
 
• Elections are held every three years for one-third of the 15-member court, ensuring continuity within the ICJ.
 
 
 
• **Qualifications for Judges**
 
 
• Judges must have a high moral character and possess the qualifications required in their respective countries for appointment to the highest judicial offices.
 
• Alternatively, they can be jurisconsults of recognized competence in international law.
 
 
 
• **Jurisdiction**
 
 
• The ICJ has jurisdiction to hear cases involving disputes between states, and it provides advisory opinions on legal questions referred to it by UN organs and specialized agencies.
 
• Only states may be parties in cases before the ICJ.

questions.question: A truck travels for 14 hours and covers the first half of the distance at the speed of 36 km/h and the remaining distance at the speed of 48 km/h. What is the total distance travelled by the truck?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A truck travels for 14 hours and covers the first half of the distance at the speed of 36 km/h and the remaining distance at the speed of 48 km/h.

**Formula used:**

Let the total distance be D km. The truck covers the first half distance \dfrac{D}{2} at 36 km/h and the remaining half distance \dfrac{D}{2} at 48 km/h.

Time = Distance / Speed

Total time = Time for first half + Time for second half

**Calculation:**

Time for first half distance = dfrac{D/2}{36} hours

Time for second half distance = dfrac{D/2}{48} hours

Total time = dfrac{D/2}{36} + dfrac{D/2}{48} hours

⇒ 14 = dfrac{D}{72} + dfrac{D}{96}

⇒ 14 = D ( dfrac{1}{72} + dfrac{1}{96} )

⇒ dfrac{1}{72} + dfrac{1}{96} = dfrac{4 + 3}{288} = dfrac{7}{288}

⇒ 14 = D times dfrac{7}{288}

⇒ D = 14 times dfrac{288}{7}

⇒ D = 576 km

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

questions.question: Which of the following comes under the concurrent list?

__
 
• The Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution includes subjects that are of interest to both the Union and the States.
 
• Forests are included in the Concurrent List to ensure both state and central governments can make laws regarding their management and conservation.
 
• This inclusion helps in maintaining ecological balance and addresses issues like deforestation and forest conservation more effectively.
 
• Both the Parliament and State Legislatures can legislate on concurrent subjects, but in case of any conflict, the central law prevails.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Police**

 
 
• Police is a subject under the State List. This means that only the state governments have the authority to legislate on matters related to the police.
 
• Each state in India has its own police force and administration.
 
 
 
• **Trade**
 
 
• Trade and commerce within the state are under the State List, while trade and commerce between different states or with foreign countries fall under the Union List.
 
• This division ensures that states can manage their internal trade, while the central government can regulate inter-state and international trade.
 
 
 
• **Defense**
 
 
• Defense is a subject under the Union List, meaning only the central government can legislate on matters related to national defense and security.
 
• This ensures a unified and consistent defense policy for the entire country.
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List**
 
 
• The Concurrent List is one of the three lists in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution that outlines the subjects on which both the state and central governments can legislate.
 
• Subjects in the Concurrent List include criminal law, marriage and divorce, bankruptcy and insolvency, and forests, among others.
 
• This list aims to ensure cooperative federalism and addresses issues that are of common interest to both the states and the union.
 
• In case of any conflict between central and state laws on a concurrent subject, the central law prevails.

__
 
• **PC Mahalanobis** is often regarded as the 'architect of Indian Planning' due to his significant role in the establishment and development of the Indian statistical system and the planning process.
 
• He was the founder of the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI), which played a crucial role in shaping India's data collection and analysis infrastructure.
 
• Mahalanobis introduced the Mahalanobis distance, a measure in statistics that is widely used in cluster analysis and classification.
 
• He was a key figure in the formulation of the Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961), which emphasized the development of heavy industries and laid the foundation for India's industrialization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• India's Five-Year Plans were centralized and integrated national economic programs, initiated in 1951 by the Planning Commission.
 
• The plans aimed to achieve rapid economic growth, self-reliance, social justice, and modernization.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956) focused on agricultural development, while the Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961) emphasized industrialization.
 
• The Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) in 2015.
 
 
 
• **Indian Statistical Institute (ISI)**
 
 
• ISI is an academic institute of national importance, founded by PC Mahalanobis in 1931 in Kolkata.
 
• It is renowned for its contributions to the fields of statistics, mathematics, and computer science.
 
• The institute conducts research and offers various academic programs, including undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral degrees.
 
• ISI has played a vital role in the development of statistical methods and their application in various sectors such as agriculture, industry, and social sciences.
 
 
 
• **Mahalanobis Distance**
 
 
• The Mahalanobis distance is a measure of the distance between a point and a distribution, introduced by PC Mahalanobis in 1936.
 
• It is widely used in multivariate statistics, pattern recognition, and cluster analysis to identify and analyze the similarity of datasets.
 
• The measure takes into account the correlations of the data set and is scale-invariant, making it a robust tool for various statistical analyses.

questions.question:
In the given circle, diameter AB is extended to meet chord CD extended at P. If the lengths of the line segments AP, CP and DP are 12 cm, 8 cm and 6 cm, respectively. what is the length of the radius of the circle?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2deba31e6db0b8a1c24fd7abdf90ab60b042e1c307713acd1193ac551d39f8a6.png]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AP = 12 cm

CP = 8 cm

DP = 6 cm

**Formula used:**

In a circle, if AB is the diameter and P is a point outside the circle, such that PA × PB = PC × PD.

**Calculation:**

Let PB = x.

Since P is outside the circle and AB is the diameter, PA × PB = PC × PD.

⇒ 12 × x = 8 × 6

⇒ 12x = 48

⇒ x = 4 cm

Now, PB = x = 4 cm.

Therefore, AB = PA - PB = 12 - 4 = 8 cm.

Since AB is the diameter of the circle, the radius of the circle is half of the diameter.

⇒ Radius = AB / 2 = 8 / 2 = 4 cm

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

• The city was discovered in the 1920s and is located in the Larkana District of Sindh, Pakistan.

questions.question: Laterite soil develops in the area with:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**high temperature and heavy rainfall**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Laterite soil is rich in iron and aluminum, formed in hot and wet tropical areas.
 
• This type of soil is the result of intense leaching due to heavy rainfall and high temperatures which accelerate the chemical weathering of rocks.
 
• Laterite soils are generally acidic in nature and have low fertility, often used for construction purposes due to their strength when dry.
 
• High temperature and heavy rainfall promote the formation of laterite soils by breaking down silicate minerals and leaving behind more insoluble minerals like iron and aluminum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Laterite Soil:**

 
 
• Laterite soils are found in regions with high rainfall and high temperatures, which are common in tropical regions such as parts of India, Southeast Asia, and Africa.
 
• These soils are characterized by their reddish color due to the high iron oxide content.
 
• Laterite soil is poor in nitrogen, potassium, lime, and humus, which makes it less suitable for agriculture without proper soil management and fertilization.
 
• In many regions, laterite soil is used for making bricks because it hardens on exposure to air.
 
 
 
• **Soil Formation:**
 
 
• Soil formation is influenced by five main factors: parent material, climate, topography, organisms, and time.
 
• Climate, particularly temperature and precipitation, is a dominant factor in the formation of laterite soil.
 
• Heavy rainfall leads to leaching, where water percolates through the soil and washes away soluble nutrients, leaving behind iron and aluminum oxides.
 
• High temperatures accelerate the chemical weathering of rocks and minerals, further contributing to the development of laterite soil.
 
 
 
• **Leaching:**
 
 
• Leaching is the process by which soluble nutrients are washed out of the soil by percolating water.
 
• This process is especially intense in regions with high rainfall, leading to the formation of nutrient-poor soils like laterite.
 
• Leaching removes essential nutrients such as calcium, magnesium, and potassium, which can affect plant growth and soil fertility.
 
• In laterite soils, leaching is responsible for the concentration of iron and aluminum oxides, which give the soil its distinctive color and properties.
 
 
 
• **Soil Management:**
 
 
• Effective soil management practices can improve the fertility of laterite soils for agricultural use.
 
• Adding organic matter, such as compost or manure, can enhance soil structure and nutrient content.
 
• Applying fertilizers that provide essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium can help support plant growth.
 
• Proper irrigation and drainage management can reduce the effects of leaching and maintain soil moisture levels.

questions.question: 28 pipes are connected to a tank. Some of them pour water into the tank, whereas the rest drain water out of it. Each of the pipes that fill water can fill the empty tank in 14 hours, whereas any of the drainpipes can empty the filled tank in 35 hours. If all the pipes are opened simultaneously when the tank is empty and the tank is filled in 2.5 hours, how many of the pipes were drainpipes?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

28 pipes are connected to a tank.

Some of them pour water into the tank, whereas the rest drain water out of it.

Each of the pipes that fill water can fill the empty tank in 14 hours.

Any of the drainpipes can empty the filled tank in 35 hours.

If all the pipes are opened simultaneously when the tank is empty and the tank is filled in 2.5 hours.

**Formula used:**

Let x be the number of filling pipes and y be the number of drainpipes.

We have x + y = 28

Filling rate of one pipe = dfrac{1}{14} tank/hour

Draining rate of one pipe = dfrac{-1}{35} tank/hour

Combined rate when all pipes are open: x times dfrac{1}{14} + y times dfrac{-1}{35}

Time taken to fill the tank = 2.5 hours

Combined rate = dfrac{1}{2.5} tank/hour

**Calculation:**

x times dfrac{1}{14} + y times dfrac{-1}{35} = dfrac{1}{2.5}

⇒ dfrac{x}{14} - dfrac{y}{35} = dfrac{1}{2.5}

⇒ dfrac{x}{14} - dfrac{y}{35} = dfrac{2}{5}

⇒ 5x - 2y = 14 times 2

⇒ 5x - 2y = 28

We also have x + y = 28

⇒ x + y = 28

Solving the two equations:

1. 5x - 2y = 28

2. x + y = 28

From equation 2: y = 28 - x

Substitute y in equation 1:

⇒ 5x - 2(28 - x) = 28

⇒ 5x - 56 + 2x = 28

⇒ 7x - 56 = 28

⇒ 7x = 84

⇒ x = 12

Therefore, y = 28 - 12

⇒ y = 16

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

• The Sutta Pitaka is one of the three main sections of the Pali Canon, the scriptures of Theravada Buddhism.
 
• It contains more than 10,000 suttas (teachings) attributed to the Buddha or his close companions.
 
• The Sutta Pitaka is divided into five Nikayas: Digha Nikaya, Majjhima Nikaya, Samyutta Nikaya, Anguttara Nikaya, and Khuddaka Nikaya.

• **Majjhima Nikaya:**

questions.question: When did Mahatma Gandhi return to India from South Africa?

• Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa on **9th January 1915**, which is commemorated as **Pravasi Bharatiya Divas** (Non-Resident Indian Day).

• He spent 21 years in South Africa, where he developed his political views, ethics, and leadership skills, particularly his advocacy for nonviolent protest (Satyagraha).
 
• Upon his return, Gandhi traveled extensively across India to understand the plight of the common people and gradually became involved in various movements against British colonial rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gandhi's Early Life and Education**

 
 
• Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, later known as Mahatma Gandhi, was born on 2nd October 1869 in Porbandar, Gujarat.
 
• He studied law at the Inner Temple in London and became a barrister in 1891.

questions.question: The radius of a sphere, 'r', is equal to the radius of the base of a right circular cone. The total volume of the two shapes = (7)/(3)πr³. If 'h' is the height of the cone, find (h)/(r).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of sphere = r

Radius of cone = r

Total volume of sphere and cone = (7)/(3)πr³

**Formula used:**

Volume of a sphere = (4)/(3)πr³

Volume of a cone = (1)/(3)πr²h

**Calculation:**

Let the volume of the sphere be (4)/(3)πr³ and the volume of the cone be (1)/(3)πr²h.

Total volume = Volume of sphere + Volume of cone

⇒ (4)/(3)πr³ + (1)/(3)πr²h = (7)/(3)πr³

Divide both sides by (1)/(3)π

⇒ 4r³ + r²h = 7r³

Subtract 4r³ from both sides:

⇒ r²h = 3r³

Divide both sides by r²:

⇒ h = 3r

⇒ (h)/(r) = 3

**∴ The value of (h)/(r) is 3.**

• The Indian Councils Act of 1909, also known as the Morley-Minto Reforms, was named after the Secretary of State for India, John Morley, and the Viceroy, Gilbert Elliot-Murray-Kynynmound, 4th Earl of Minto.
 
• The Act introduced a separate electorate system for Muslims, allowing them to elect their representatives through separate electorates.
 
• It aimed to involve more Indians in the governance process by expanding the legislative councils and increasing the number of elected members.
 
• This reform was a response to the growing demand for greater participation of Indians in the administration and was seen as an attempt to placate the Indian National Congress and other political groups.
 
 
 
• **Separate Electorates**
 
 
• Separate electorates refer to a system where different communities vote separately for their representatives.
 
• In the context of the Indian Councils Act of 1909, it meant that Muslims could elect their representatives separately from the rest of the population.
 
• This system was introduced to address the concerns of the Muslim community regarding adequate representation in the legislative bodies.
 
• The introduction of separate electorates was a significant development in the Indian political landscape and had long-term implications for communal relations in India.
 
 
 
• **Communal Representation**
 
 
• Communal representation refers to the allocation of political representation based on religious or ethnic communities.
 
• In colonial India, communal representation was introduced to ensure that minority communities, like Muslims, had a voice in the legislative process.
 
• This was seen as a way to protect the interests of minority communities and prevent their domination by the majority community.
 
• However, communal representation also had the effect of deepening communal divisions and was a contentious issue in Indian politics.

• The Lok Sabha is responsible for passing the Finance Bill and has significant control over financial matters.

• **Finance Bill:**

• It encompasses all the legislative proposals for the imposition of new taxes, modification of existing tax structures, or abolition of taxes as proposed in the Budget.
 
• A Finance Bill must be passed by Parliament and assented to by the President before it becomes law.
 
• There are two types of Finance Bills: Money Bills and Financial Bills. Money Bills solely deal with national taxation and government spending, while Financial Bills may include other matters as well.

questions.question: If 231 × 326 = 75306, then what is the value of 2.31 × 0.326?
questions.solution:

2.31 × 0.326

**Approach:**

1. Count the decimal places:

In 2.31, there is 1 decimal place.

In 0.326, there are 3 decimal places.

Total decimal places = 1 + 3 = 4.

2. Multiply the numbers without considering the decimal points:

231 × 326 = 75306

3. Place the decimal point:

Since there are 4 decimal places in total, we place the decimal point 4 places from the right in the product.

⇒ 2.31 × 0.326 = 0.75306

**∴ The value of 2.31 × 0.326 is 0.75306.**

questions.question: Rainbow is a natural phenomenon which shows:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**dispersion**__.

__
 
• A rainbow is formed due to the **dispersion of light** when it passes through water droplets in the atmosphere.
 
• Dispersion causes the white sunlight to split into its constituent colors (VIBGYOR - Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, and Red).
 
• The process of dispersion involves the **bending of light** rays at different angles when they enter and exit the water droplets, resulting in a spectrum of colors.
 
• The phenomenon of a rainbow can be observed when the sun is low in the sky and behind the observer, and rain is falling in front of them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diffraction**

 
 
• Diffraction is the bending of light waves around the edges of an obstacle or aperture.
 
• This phenomenon occurs with all types of waves, including light, sound, and water waves.
 
• An example of diffraction is the spreading of light when it passes through a small slit.
 
 
 
• **Refraction**
 
 
• Refraction is the change in direction of light when it passes from one medium to another of different density.
 
• This bending of light is due to the change in speed of light in different mediums.
 
• An example of refraction is the bending of light when it passes from air into water, making objects appear bent or distorted.
 
 
 
• **Reflection**
 
 
• Reflection is the bouncing back of light rays when they hit a surface.
 
• The angle of incidence (incoming angle) is equal to the angle of reflection (outgoing angle).
 
• An example of reflection is the image seen in a mirror.

questions.question: Article 371-A of the Constitution of India provides special status to the state of ______.

• Article 371-A of the Indian Constitution provides special provisions for the state of **Nagaland** to ensure the protection and preservation of the Naga culture and traditions.
 
• It was incorporated into the Constitution through the **13th Amendment Act of 1962**.
 
• This article ensures that no Act of Parliament in respect of religious or social practices of the Nagas, Naga customary law and procedure, administration of civil and criminal justice involving decisions according to Naga customary law, and ownership and transfer of land and its resources shall apply to Nagaland unless the Legislative Assembly of Nagaland by a resolution so decides.

questions.question: An article sold at a gain of 10% yields ₹150 more than when sold at a loss of 10%. Its cost price is:

An article sold at a gain of 10% yields ₹150 more than when sold at a loss of 10%

Let the cost price be ₹C.

Selling price at 10% gain = C + 0.1C = 1.1C

Selling price at 10% loss = C - 0.1C = 0.9C

Difference in selling prices = 1.1C - 0.9C = 0.2C

0.2C = ₹150

⇒ C = ₹150 / 0.2

⇒ C = ₹750

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

• **Bodh Gaya** is a religious site and place of pilgrimage associated with the Mahabodhi Temple Complex in Gaya district in the Indian state of Bihar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Drought Prone Areas Programme (DPAP)**

 
 
• The Drought Prone Areas Programme (DPAP) is one of the oldest area development programmes in India, started in 1973.

questions.question: When is 'International Day of Sign Languages' celebrated annually across the world?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**23rd September**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The International Day of Sign Languages is celebrated annually on **23rd September**.
 
• This date was chosen to commemorate the establishment of the World Federation of the Deaf (WFD) on 23 September 1951.
 
• The day was first celebrated in 2018 as part of the International Week of the Deaf.
 
• The aim is to raise awareness of the importance of sign languages in the full realization of the human rights of people who are deaf.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **World Federation of the Deaf (WFD)**

 
 
• WFD is an international non-governmental organization that represents approximately 70 million deaf people worldwide.
 
• It was established in Rome, Italy, on 23 September 1951.
 
• WFD's mission is to promote the human rights of deaf people and ensure they have equal opportunities.
 
 
 
• **International Week of the Deaf (IWD)**
 
 
• It is an initiative of the WFD and is celebrated annually by the global deaf community during the last full week of September.
 
• The week culminates with the International Day of Sign Languages on 23rd September.
 
• The aim is to draw attention to the achievements and challenges of the deaf community.
 
 
 
• **Sign Languages**
 
 
• Sign languages are fully-fledged natural languages with their own grammar and lexicon.
 
• They are primarily used by deaf communities around the world.
 
• Recognizing and promoting the use of sign languages can help ensure the inclusion and participation of deaf people in society.
 
 
 
• **Human Rights of Deaf People**
 
 
• Ensuring the human rights of deaf people includes access to education, employment, public services, and cultural life in sign language.
 
• Promoting sign languages helps eliminate barriers and fosters the full and equal participation of deaf people in society.
